paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: Suppose it is proposed that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal in terms of its necessity and practicality. You will have 30 minutes to write the response. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 方向：假设建议要求大学生参加至少一项研究项目。您现在需要写一份回复，说明您对该提案的必要性和实用性的看法。您将有 30 分钟的时间来撰写回复。您应该写至少 120 个字但不超过 180 个字。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, there is a passage with ten blanks. You are required to select one word for each blank from a list of choices given in a word bank following the passage. Read the passage through carefully before making your choices. Each choice in the bank is identified by a letter. Please mark the corresponding letter for each item on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre. You may not use any of the words in the bank more than once.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，有一段有十个空格。您需要从文章后面的单词库中给出的选项列表中为每个空白选择一个单词。在做出选择之前仔细阅读该段落。银行中的每个选择都由一个字母标识。请在答题卡 2 上的每个项目上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。您不得多次使用银行中的任何单词。

paragraphs.sourceText: Junk-food lovers who try to cut back on fries or chocolate may experience symptoms similar to drug withdrawal, a new study suggests.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一项新的研究表明，尝试减少薯条或巧克力的垃圾食品爱好者可能会出现类似于药物戒断的症状。

paragraphs.sourceText: Researchers found that people attempting to cut down on eating highly processed foods experience some of the same 26 and psychological symptoms — such as mood swings, anxiety, headaches and poor sleep — as those 27 smoking cigarettes or using drugs, according to the study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究人员发现，试图减少高度加工食品摄入的人会经历一些与戒烟或吸毒者相同的身体和心理症状，例如情绪波动、焦虑、头痛和睡眠质量不佳。

paragraphs.sourceText: The new study 28 the first evidence that these withdrawal-like symptoms can occur when people cut down on highly processed foods, said lead study author Erica Schulte.
paragraphs.translationZh: 该研究的主要作者埃丽卡·舒尔特 (Erica Schulte) 表示，这项新研究首次提供了证据，表明当人们减少高度加工食品的摄入量时，可能会出现这些戒断症状。

paragraphs.sourceText: Based on the participants’ self-reported symptoms, withdrawal symptoms were 29 more intense between the second and fifth days after attempting to reduce junk-food consumption, which 30 the time span people live through during drug withdrawal.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据参与者自我报告的症状，在尝试减少垃圾食品消费后的第二天到第五天，戒断症状明显更加严重，这与人们在戒毒期间经历的时间跨度相当。

paragraphs.sourceText: The idea that food may be addictive after “heavy” use by some individuals is a 31 subject, Schulte said. Although prior studies in animals and humans have shown some biological and behavioral similarities between substance-use disorders and addictive-like consumption of highly processed foods, no studies have looked at whether reducing junk food can 32 withdrawal symptoms in people, she noted. Raising 33 that people may experience irritability (烦躁) or headaches when cutting down on junk food can help individuals 34 coping strategies in advance, Schulte noted. The findings may also 35 light on the barriers people face when changing eating habits — barriers that may play a role in people dropping out of treatments, she said.
paragraphs.translationZh: 舒尔特说，某些人“大量”食用食物后可能会上瘾的想法是一个有争议的话题。她指出，尽管之前对动物和人类的研究表明，物质使用障碍和高度加工食品的成瘾性消费之间存在一些生物学和行为相似性，但没有研究探讨减少垃圾食品是否会引发人们的戒断症状。舒尔特指出，提高人们对减少垃圾食品摄入量时可能会出现烦躁或头痛的认识，可以帮助人们提前准备应对策略。她说，这些发现还可能揭示人们在改变饮食习惯时面临的障碍——这些障碍可能会导致人们放弃治疗。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Giving a better phone interview
paragraphs.translationZh: 提供更好的电话面试

paragraphs.sourceText: A) These days, phone interviews are an unavoidable part of the job interview process, and for good reason: They save time and effort. But that doesn’t mean that phone calls require zero energy on the part of the candidate. Many companies treat phone screening as the official first round of the hiring process. That means candidates are expected to go into them prepared with as much information as possible about the company, position, and their own skills and strengths.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答）如今，电话面试是求职面试过程中不可避免的一部分，这是有充分理由的：它们节省时间和精力。但这并不意味着打电话对候选人来说需要零精力。许多公司将电话筛选视为正式的第一轮招聘流程。这意味着候选人应在面试中准备尽可能多的有关公司、职位以及自己的技能和优势的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) A big mistake people often make is talking about their personal lives. Don’t talk about your personal life unless you’re directly asked a question about what you like to do in your off-hours. “The point of a phone interview is to focus on getting to know a candidate’s professional experience and goals,” says McKenzie Roark, campus talent specialist at Lithko Contracting. “A recruiter is trying to see if they are the best fit for a role, and learning about their personal life doesn’t help. For example, when asked where you see yourself in five years, we don’t want to know that you hope to be married or that you want to buy a new house. That is nice, but that isn’t relative to anything professional.”
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 人们经常犯的一个大错误是谈论他们的个人生活。不要谈论你的个人生活，除非你被直接问到你在下班时间喜欢做什么的问题。 “电话面试的重点是了解候选人的专业经验和目标，”Lithko Contracting 的校园人才专家麦肯齐·罗克 (McKenzie Roark) 说。 “招聘人员试图了解他们是否最适合某个职位，了解他们的个人生活并没有帮助。例如，当被问及你对五年后的自己有何看法时，我们不想知道你希望结婚或想买新房。这很好，但这与任何职业无关。”

paragraphs.sourceText: C) It might be tempting to cross something off your to-do list while on a phone interview, but recruiters and hiring managers can easily tell if your attention is elsewhere. Many interviewers are annoyed to see people who decide to multitask while on the phone interview. There are candidates who wash dishes, go for walks, or do grocery shopping during the interview. Needless to say, this doesn’t reflect well on your level of interest in the position you’re interviewing for.
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 在电话面试时，你可能会很想从待办事项清单上划掉一些事情，但招聘人员和招聘经理可以很容易地判断出你的注意力是否在其他地方。许多面试官对在电话面试时决定同时处理多项任务的人感到恼火。有些候选人在面试期间洗碗、散步或去杂货店购物。不用说，这并不能很好地反映您对所面试职位的兴趣程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) The question regarding pay is also best avoided. To be frank, it’s simply too early in the process for you to be the one who brings up salary expectations. “Chances are if a candidate is participating in a phone interview, this is the first time they have talked with the company, and the first call isn’t the appropriate time to talk about ‘what’s in it for you,’ ” says Justina Strnad, the Talent Acquisition Manager for Shiftgig. “Trust me, if you are a great candidate and make it to the next step, the hiring team is going to be very transparent about what’s in it for you later on.”
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 关于薪酬的问题也最好避免。坦率地说，对于你来说，现在提出薪资期望还为时过早。 Shiftgig 的人才招聘经理贾斯蒂娜·斯特纳德 (Justina Strnad) 表示：“如果应聘者参加电话面试，这很可能是他们第一次与公司交谈，而第一次通话并不是谈论‘这对你有什么好处’的合适时机。” “相信我，如果你是一个优秀的候选人并进入下一步，招聘团队将会非常透明地告诉你以后能为你带来什么。”

paragraphs.sourceText: E) “After wrapping up a phone interview, it is typical that the interviewer will ask the candidate if they have any questions. I can’t stress this enough: ALWAYS ask questions,” says Roark. “If we have had a great phone interview and then we wrap up and they don’t have any questions for me, it pretty much ruins the whole interview. It tells me that the candidate is uninterested in the role, which in reality might not be the case at all,” she notes. But surely, if you’re interested in a job, you can think of something to ask your interviewer.
paragraphs.translationZh: E) “电话面试结束后，面试官通常会询问应聘者是否有任何问题。这一点我再怎么强调也不为过：永远要问问题，”罗克说。 “如果我们进行了一次很棒的电话面试，然后我们结束了，而他们没有向我提出任何问题，那么这几乎会毁掉整个面试。这告诉我，候选人对这个职位不感兴趣，而实际上情况可能根本不是这样，”她指出。但当然，如果你对某份工作感兴趣，你可以想出一些问题来问你的面试官。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) It seems basic, but surprisingly, a lot of people are late to phone interviews. “About a quarter of the people with whom I schedule phone interviews aren’t on time,” says Sophie Cikovsky, who handles U.S. recruiting for Infinite Global. “While this bothers me personally, it’s also indicative of someone who isn’t very detail-oriented,” she explains. “In order to identify this early in the hiring process, I started asking all candidates a few years ago to call me as opposed to calling them at an agreed-upon time. That way, if I hear from them at 1:13 pm or 12:49 pm instead of our planned 1:00 pm interview time, I have an early indicator that they might not be a great fit.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 这看起来很简单，但令人惊讶的是，很多人电话面试都迟到了。 “在我安排的电话面试中，约有四分之一的人没有准时，”负责 Infinite Global 美国招聘的索菲·奇科夫斯基 (Sophie Cikovsky) 说道。 “虽然这让我个人感到困扰，但这也表明这个人不太注重细节，”她解释道。 “为了在招聘过程中尽早发现这一点，我在几年前开始要求所有候选人给我打电话，而不是在约定的时间给他们打电话。这样，如果我在下午 1:13 或 12:49 而不是我们计划的下午 1:00 面试时间收到他们的来信，我就能尽早发现他们可能不太合适。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) “Make sure you test your headset and connection before dialing in,” recommends Roark. “There is nothing more frustrating for a recruiter who has a structured interview guide in place having to repeatedly ask the same question over and over because they could not understand your answer due to dropped signals.” Test-call a friend beforehand, or even call yourself from a landline if necessary; it will take less than a minute.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) “请确保在拨入之前测试耳机和连接，”Roark 建议。 “对于拥有结构化面试指南的招聘人员来说，没有什么比这更令人沮丧的了，他们不得不一遍又一遍地重复问同样的问题，因为由于信号丢失，他们无法理解你的答案。”提前给朋友打电话，如有必要，甚至可以用固定电话给自己打电话；这将需要不到一分钟的时间。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) You might be eager to get your point across or talk about your experience, but interrupting the interviewer is awkward and rude. Interviewing can be stressful, and sometimes that stress manifests itself in speaking too fast, speaking too loud, talking over the interviewer, or attempting to answer the interviewer’s question before they have actually finished asking the question,” says Chris Dardis, a recruiting expert. “Don’t do this.” There’s a big difference between being assertive (自信的) and being aggressive, and interviewers can always recognize it.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 你可能渴望表达自己的观点或谈论你的经历，但打断面试官是尴尬和粗鲁的。面试可能会带来压力，有时这种压力表现为说得太快、太大声、凌驾于面试官之上，或者在面试官真正问完问题之前就试图回答他们的问题，”招聘专家克里斯·达迪斯 (Chris Dardis) 说，“不要这样做。”自信和进取之间有很大的区别，面试官总能认出这一点。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) It’s tough not to say things like “um” “uh” and “like” in everyday speech, but these verbal habits become much more pronounced when speaking on the phone, says Dardis. “In face-to-face interviews, they’re not as noticeable, because there are other things like your hair, suit, or body language to distract people.” But in a phone interview, the only thing you have to go on is what you say and how you say it. “That’s why it’s so important to eliminate these words from your speech when doing a phone interview.”
paragraphs.translationZh: I）达迪斯说，在日常言语中很难不说“嗯”“呃”和“喜欢”之类的东西，但这些语言习惯在打电话时变得更加明显。 “在面对面的采访中，它们并不那么引人注目，因为还有其他东西，比如你的头发、西装或肢体语言，会分散人们的注意力。”但在电话面试中，你唯一需要做的就是你说什么以及如何说。 “这就是为什么在电话采访时从演讲中删除这些词是如此重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Not knowing anything about the company or job you’re interviewing for is way more obvious than you’d think. “Many people think that they don’t have to put as much effort into researching the role or the company,” says Steve Prichard, an HR consultant. And if you have your laptop in front of you during the interview to do a few quick searches, they won’t know the difference, right? Not exactly. “Seasoned interviewers will know whether an interviewee is researching while on the phone. The interviewer can often even hear the typing as they ask the question,” he adds.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 对你正在面试的公司或工作一无所知比你想象的要明显得多。 “许多人认为他们不必花太多精力来研究这个职位或公司，”人力资源顾问史蒂夫·普里查德 (Steve Prichard) 说。如果您在面试期间将笔记本电脑放在面前进行一些快速搜索，他们就不会知道其中的区别，对吗？不完全是。 “经验丰富的面试官会知道受访者是否在打电话时进行研究。面试官甚至在提问时甚至可以听到打字声，”他补充道。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) “The key to success during a phone interview is clear and concise answers,” says Dardis. “People’s attention spans tend to be shorter over the phone. You don’t want your future employer to lose interest in the conversation.” He recommends practicing answers to questions you know will be asked ahead of time in order to be clear on what you’re going to say. That way, you can prevent talking in an aimless manner.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) “电话面试成功的关键是清晰简洁的答案，”达迪斯说。 “人们在电话中的注意力往往会较短。你不希望你未来的雇主对谈话失去兴趣。”他建议提前练习回答你知道会被问到的问题，以便清楚你要说什么。这样，你就可以防止漫无目的地说话。

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. Interviewees are advised not to ask questions about pay during a phone interview.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 建议受访者在电话面试期间不要询问有关薪酬的问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. Experienced interviewers will know if an applicant is searching for information online while talking on the phone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37. 有经验的面试官会知道申请人在打电话时是否在网上搜索信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38. Many employers regard the phone interview as the first step of the official recruiting process.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38. 许多雇主将电话面试视为正式招聘流程的第一步。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39. Applicants who don’t ask questions at the end of an interview most probably ruin their chance of getting the position.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39. 面试结束时不提问的申请人很可能会毁掉获得该职位的机会。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40. The interviewee should test their phone connection before they call the interviewer.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40. 受访者在致电采访者之前应测试电话连接。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41. It is annoying to the interviewer to find the applicant doing other tasks while being interviewed.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41. 面试官发现应聘者在接受面试时在做其他事情，这让面试官很恼火。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42. To pass a phone interview, the most important thing is to answer questions clearly and concisely.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42. 要通过电话面试，最重要的是清楚、简洁地回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43. If you fail to call the interviewer on time, they might not see you as a suitable candidate.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43. 如果您没有按时给面试官打电话，他们可能不会认为您是合适的候选人。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44. Applicants should avoid talking about their personal lives if the interviewer has only asked about their professional background and goals.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44. 如果面试官只询问申请人的职业背景和目标，申请人应避免谈论他们的个人生活。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45. It is impolite for an interviewee to interrupt the interviewer in the phone conversation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 受访者在电话交谈中打断采访者是不礼貌的。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A, B, C and D. You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A、B、C 和 D。您应该决定最佳选项，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Disgust is a universal human emotion. One type of disgust is called physical disgust, which protects us from eating or touching things that could be dangerous for us, such as raw meat or insects. Children experience physical disgust from a very early age, but do not achieve an understanding of the concept until they are around four years old.
paragraphs.translationZh: 厌恶是人类普遍的情感。一种厌恶称为身体厌恶，它可以保护我们避免吃或触摸可能对我们有危险的东西，例如生肉或昆虫。孩子们从很小的时候就经历了身体上的厌恶，但直到四岁左右才理解这个概念。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some researchers maintain that there is another type of disgust, called moral disgust, that protects us from engaging in activities that can be perceived as morally wrong. Examples of moral disgust are stealing, lying or cheating.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一些研究人员认为，还有另一种厌恶，称为道德厌恶，它可以保护我们不从事可能被视为道德错误的活动。道德厌恶的例子有偷窃、撒谎或欺骗。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, not all academics think that moral disgust really exists. Some say that when we refer to disgust in relation to moral issues, we are using disgust as a metaphor (隐喻), and what we are feeling is in reality anger.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，并非所有学者都认为道德厌恶确实存在。有人说，当我们在道德问题上提到厌恶时，我们是用厌恶来比喻，我们感受到的实际上是愤怒。

paragraphs.sourceText: If moral disgust appears quite late in development, it makes sense to think that there is actually a social component to it. Children learn about emotions in many different ways. Of special relevance are parents-children conversations about emotions. Indeed, children whose parents talk about emotions often have a better emotional understanding than children whose parents do not discuss emotions often.
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果道德厌恶在发展过程中出现得很晚，那么认为它实际上有社会成分是有道理的。孩子们通过多种不同的方式了解情绪。特别重要的是父母与孩子关于情感的对话。事实上，父母谈论情感的孩子往往比父母不经常谈论情感的孩子有更好的情感理解能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: However, there are no studies that have examined how parents and children talk about disgust. This is what we set up to examine in our study.
paragraphs.translationZh: 然而，还没有研究调查父母和孩子如何谈论厌恶。这就是我们在研究中要检查的内容。

paragraphs.sourceText: We asked 68 English-speaking mothers and their four-, six-, or eight-year-old children to discuss some stories about moral and physical disgust. Our preliminary findings show mothers and children do talk about disgust, but mainly about physical disgust and not so much about moral disgust.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们采访了 68 位说英语的母亲和她们四岁、六岁或八岁的孩子，讨论了一些关于道德和身体厌恶的故事。我们的初步调查结果显示，母亲和孩子确实会谈论厌恶，但主要是身体上的厌恶，而不是道德上的厌恶。

paragraphs.sourceText: When we asked mothers and children to discuss moral issues, such as whether it is OK to play with a child who has stolen someone else’s snack, they linked this type of moral wrongdoing with the emotion of anger and not disgust.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我们要求母亲和孩子讨论道德问题时，例如与偷了别人零食的孩子一起玩是否可以，他们将这种道德不当行为与愤怒而不是厌恶情绪联系起来。

paragraphs.sourceText: Does this mean that moral disgust does not exist? Some researchers suggest moral disgust exists in adults. Our findings suggest that moral disgust is either understood at a later age or is only used metaphorically, if at all, in children as old as eight years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这是否意味着道德厌恶不存在？一些研究人员认为成年人存在道德厌恶。我们的研究结果表明，对于八岁的孩子来说，道德厌恶要么是在以后的年龄才被理解，要么只是隐喻地使用（如果有的话）。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. What does the passage tell us about physical disgust?
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 关于身体厌恶，这段经文告诉我们什么？

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. How do some researchers perceive moral disgust?
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 一些研究人员如何看待道德厌恶？

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. Why does moral disgust appear quite late in children’s development?

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: After finding out details about a stranger, we mistakenly think that they also know about us. As a result, we act more honestly around them, according to a recent study in Nature.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在了解了陌生人的详细信息后，我们错误地认为他们也了解我们。根据《自然》杂志最近的一项研究，我们在面对这些问题时会更加诚实地行事。

paragraphs.sourceText: Past research has found that we tend to assume social relationships are reciprocal (相互的). Most of the time, this assumption is accurate: someone you think of as a friend will usually consider you a friend too. But sometimes our social ties are more one-sided: for example, you might learn something about a stranger who doesn’t know you at all. Researchers Anuj Shah and Michael LaForest wondered whether our tendency to believe that social ties are reciprocal could lead us to mistakenly feel that a stranger does actually know us.
paragraphs.translationZh: 过去的研究发现，我们倾向于假设社会关系是相互的。大多数时候，这个假设是准确的：你认为是朋友的人通常也会认为你是朋友。但有时我们的社会关系更加片面：例如，您可能会了解到一位根本不认识您的陌生人的一些信息。研究人员阿努吉·沙阿（Anuj Shah）和迈克尔·拉福雷斯特（Michael LaForest）想知道，我们相信社会关系是相互的倾向是否会导致我们错误地认为陌生人确实认识我们。

paragraphs.sourceText: In a series of lab-based studies, this is exactly what the researchers found. When we know about strangers, we erroneously think they also know about us. But the really interesting finding came when the researchers stepped out of the lab, to conduct a field experiment. The team developed leaflets (传单) containing fairly ordinary information about local community police officers, such as their favourite food, hobbies, or reasons for joining the police force. They then sent out these leaflets to every apartment in a number of housing developments in disadvantaged areas. The officers themselves also dropped off cards to local residents containing similar information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在一系列基于实验室的研究中，这正是研究人员发现的。当我们了解陌生人时，我们错误地认为他们也了解我们。但当研究人员走出实验室进行现场实验时，真正有趣的发现出现了。该团队制作了传单，其中包含当地社区警察的相当普通的信息，例如他们最喜欢的食物、爱好或加入警察部队的原因。然后，他们将这些传单分发到贫困地区多个住房开发项目的每套公寓。官员们还向当地居民发放了包含类似信息的卡片。

paragraphs.sourceText: Two months later, the researchers surveyed residents at these housing developments as well as control areas that did not receive leaflets or outreach cards. Residents were asked to imagine that they had committed a crime and how likely it would be that local officers would find out about it. They also rated how well the officers in the area knew them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 两个月后，研究人员对这些住房开发区以及没有收到传单或外展卡的控制区的居民进行了调查。居民被要求想象他们犯了罪，以及当地官员发现这件事的可能性有多大。他们还评估了该地区官员对他们的了解程度。

paragraphs.sourceText: The team found that residents of the developments that had received the leaflets believed it more likely that local officers would find out about illegal activity than residents of the control areas. Even more strikingly, the team found that immediately after the leaflet distribution, there were fewer criminal complaints and arrests in the areas around the developments that had received the leaflets than around the control developments.
paragraphs.translationZh: 研究小组发现，收到传单的开发区居民认为，当地官员比控制区居民更有可能发现非法活动。更引人注目的是，研究小组发现，在散发传单后，收到传单的开发项目周围地区的刑事投诉和逮捕数量比控制开发项目周围的要少。
